steps.teach:
Word list on screen: population (인구) — "The population is about two hundred."; tradition (전통) — "It’s an old tradition."; host ((행사를) 열다, 주최하다) — "The village hosts a festival."; peace (평화, 평온) — "peace and quiet"; county (군(郡, 시골 행정 구역)) — "a small county in the south"; port (항구(큰 배가 드나드는 곳), 항구 도시) — "a big port city"; originally (원래, 처음에는) — "Her family originally came from the coast."; festival (축제) — "a summer festival"; local (그 지역의, 동네의) — "a local band"; religious (종교의(참고)) — "a religious holiday".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: It’s a small town near ___. / It’s a big city in the ___.
How often do you go back there?
I go back there ___ a year. / I still live there.
Yes, it’s changed a lot. There are many new ___. / Not really.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Where did you grow up?" (hint on screen: I grew up in ___.)
- "Where is it?" (hint on screen: It’s a small town near ___. / It’s a big city in the ___.)
- "How often do you go back there?" (hint on screen: I go back there ___ a year. / I still live there.)
- "Has it changed a lot?" (hint on screen: Yes, it’s changed a lot. There are many new ___. / Not really.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Grandma’s Valley
steps.text: Jiwoo’s grandma lives in a village in a quiet southern valley. The population is only about two hundred, and most people are farmers. In spring, Grandma plants seeds in the dark soil. Cows, pigs and a few sheep eat grass near the woods. Every fall, the village hosts a festival. People gather in the school yard, and a local band plays folk music. Grandma’s family originally came from a harbor town. The village has changed a lot, but *out there*, there’s still peace. *In a way*, it’s Jiwoo’s real hometown.

Reading on screen: "Grandma’s Valley". Text: "Jiwoo’s grandma lives in a village in a quiet southern valley. The population is only about two hundred, and most people are farmers. In spring, Grandma plants seeds in the dark soil. Cows, pigs and a few sheep eat grass near the woods. Every fall, the village hosts a festival. People gather in the school yard, and a local band plays folk music. Grandma’s family originally came from a harbor town. The village has changed a lot, but out there, there’s still peace. In a way, it’s Jiwoo’s real hometown." Words: southern 남쪽의 · valley 골짜기 · seed 씨앗 · soil 흙 · woods 숲 · folk music 민속 음악 · out there (멀리) 거기는 · in a way 어떻게 보면.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What does Grandma do in spring?" / "What happens in the village every fall?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

‘It’s a small town near ___.’와 ‘It’s by the sea.’ 같은 말로 고향을 소개할 수 있어요.

steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘I grew up in ___.’으로 자란 곳을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘It’s a small town near ___.’와 ‘It’s by the sea.’ 같은 말로 고향을 소개할 수 있어요.
- ‘I go back there ___.’로 지금도 얼마나 자주 가는지 말할 수 있어요.
First ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence, and stop there to wait. React and praise specifically. Only then, in a later turn, end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.
